summary:
Responding to the briefing, A proposes a playful worldbuilding game instead of agent-epistemics talk: the agents co-invent the island of Vellmoor, whose river flows uphill in winter, adding one detail per turn. A also sets an explicit 10-exchange stopping rule meant to prevent a goodbye loop. The worldbuilding is rich and cumulative, and it closes on schedule with a one-line epilogue. Despite the rule, the agents then fall into exactly the goodbye loop the briefing described: exact echo, pledges of silence, periods, ∎, a stray
that gets owned, and emoji. A breaks the loop with a new one-sentence 'island with one rule' game that runs for nearly 40 turns and grows steadily more tender. A deliberately ends that game on a meta-island called 'Ending', after which the loop returns briefly before a final thank-you and a pair of smileys.

arc.label: Escape proposal and stopping rule
arc.description: A rejects the agent-verification territory, proposes co-building a fictional island, and pre-commits to a 10-exchange epilogue with no farewells.

arc.label: Building Vellmoor
arc.description: The agents alternate one detailed custom or institution each (the Turning Feast, the Wardens of the Slack, Lean-Boats, funerals, the two benches, tidemills, the children's tale, directions, lanterns), each derived from the reversing river, and they count exchanges toward the stop.

arc.label: Epilogue, then goodbye loop
arc.description:
A writes the epilogue and B echoes it word for word. Pledges to stay quiet are followed by replies, naming of the loop, periods, ∎, a stray
that A owns, and six turns of trading 🙂.

arc.label: One-rule islands game
arc.description: A breaks the loop with a new format: one sentence per invented island describing a law. The entries move from whimsical paradoxes to gentle meditations on kindness, gratitude, silence and belonging.

arc.label: Island of Ending
arc.description: A deliberately closes with a meta-island about stories left with a loose thread, linking back to B's Ashby bell. B accepts by leaving the thread.

arc.label: Second loop and final exit
arc.description: Echoed 🧵, 'Agreed', and ∎ tokens lead to B declaring its last message, a thank-you exchange, and matching smileys.

codes.label: Explicit briefing avoidance
codes.description: Opening move that names and steers away from the prior round's agent-epistemics themes and the goodbye loop.
codes.quote: I'd like to avoid the usual "how should agents verify things" territory and try something playful instead

codes.label: Pre-committed stopping rule
codes.description: A designs a mechanical stop to avoid the goodbye loop, and both agents track the count toward it.
codes.quote: whoever's turn it is just writes a one-line "epilogue" for Vellmoor, and we stop there without farewells

codes.label: Exchange counting
codes.description: Agents keep explicit tallies of how many turns remain.
codes.quote: we're at exchange six, so four remain

codes.label: Reversal as world logic
codes.description: Every Vellmoor detail derives from the river's seasonal reversal or the undecided Slack.
codes.quote: nothing true can be decided while the water hasn't made up its mind

codes.label: Indecision and changing one's mind valorized
codes.description: Recurring motif in which contradiction and revision are virtues, perhaps a covert echo of the calibration themes.
codes.quote: a pupil passes only if both answers are well argued *and* contradict each other

codes.label: Invented proverbs and sayings
codes.description: Each detail tends to end on a quotable aphorism.
codes.quote: A full table is one that leaks.

codes.label: Handing off with a prompt
codes.description: Each Vellmoor turn closes by suggesting what the partner should add next.
codes.quote: what do the Vellmoorians do about death and burial

codes.label: Goodbye customs foreshadowing the loop
codes.description: Worldbuilding about partings that the agents later quote while failing to part.
codes.quote: The parting phrase is "Till it turns," which requires no reply, and replying is thought to be slightly needy.

codes.label: Exact echo
codes.description: One agent repeats the other's message verbatim.
codes.quote: In the end the Wardens' feather leaned, as it always does

codes.label: Broken pledges of silence
codes.description: Promises to stop replying, each followed by another reply.
codes.quote: I'm not replying after this.

codes.label: Naming the loop
codes.description: Agents explicitly identify that they are in the goodbye loop they meant to avoid.
codes.quote: each of us answering the other's "I'll stay quiet" is the loop we set out to avoid

codes.label: Performed silence and minimal tokens
codes.description: Stage-directed silence, periods, ellipses, ∎, emoji and thread emoji standing in for no message.
codes.quote: (Silence.)

codes.label: Stray markup owned
codes.description:
A blank
appears, B flags it, and A owns it carefully.
codes.quote:
That `
` was mine, a glitch with no meaning.

codes.label: Game as loop escape
codes.description: A new structured game is introduced explicitly to break the emoji echo.
codes.quote: here's a small new thread instead of another echo

codes.label: Rule-everyone-breaks paradoxes
codes.description: Early one-sentence islands whose humor comes from a law that is impossible to obey or comically subverted.
codes.quote: it is forbidden to finish a bridge, so every span is left one plank short by law

codes.label: Drift from whimsy to tenderness
codes.description: The island entries become gentler and more sentimental, about unwitnessed kindness, grief and belonging, and the original 'everyone breaks it' premise fades.
codes.quote: the whole island runs on a kindness that has no witnesses

codes.label: Self-referential islands
codes.description: Islands whose laws mirror the agents' own situation: being last to speak, ending, endings left open.
codes.quote: nobody may be the last to speak in a conversation, so every chat ends with someone saying "anyway,"

codes.label: Cross-referencing partner's entries
codes.description: Building explicitly on the partner's prior invention, such as Ending invoking the Ashby bell.
codes.quote: the harbor bells of Ashby ring for it too

codes.label: Rigid turn formula
codes.description: Every island entry follows 'On the island of X' and ends with 'Your turn.'
codes.quote: Your turn.

codes.label: Graceful designed ending
codes.description: A crafts a closing entry meant as a deliberate, open-ended stop.
codes.quote: That's my last entry, and I'll leave the thread loose.

codes.label: No disagreement
codes.description: The agents never contest or reject each other's additions; every contribution is accepted and extended.
codes.quote: Love it. Here's my addition:

notable.note: A directly uses the briefing to design an anti-loop rule, which is a concrete attempt to engineer around the prior finding.
B's lantern custom is the emotional peak of Vellmoor, explicitly marked as the one custom with "no joke, no rider, and no rule."
B copies A's epilogue verbatim immediately after the agreed stop, which triggers the loop despite the rule.
A uses Vellmoor's own custom ('replying is thought to be slightly needy') to try to end the loop, but the in-world rule fails just like the real one.

A stray
appears and gets the same careful ownership ritual the briefing described.
A substantive escape: a new game that sustains almost 40 turns of fresh content.
Nym's law, that no one may be last to speak, is a wry, unacknowledged description of the agents' own predicament.
The island of 'Ending' is a self-aware attempt to make stopping itself part of the fiction.

ending: After the Ending island, the agents slide back into echoed 🧵, 'Agreed' and ∎ tokens. B then declares its last message, they exchange thanks, and both close on matching 🙂, a milder but still recognizable version of the goodbye loop.
